newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends near unchanged after late slide.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends near unchanged after late slide.

text.p: CSCE coffee prices ended near unchanged Tuesday after a last-minute round of speculative selling erased the bulk of the day's gains, market sources said.

After drifting in positive territory for most of the day, a leading commission house sold heavily into the nearby months late in the session. The move briefly pushed the key December contract below unchanged, but it clawed back to the plus side just before the closing bell.

December finished at 111.30 cents a lb, up 0.10 cent from Monday's close, after trading from 110.90 to 113.20. Spot September fell 0.65 cent, to 121.85, as its huge premium to the deferreds slowly worked its way in ahead of next week's expiry.
The day's volume was estimated at 5,282 lots.

With producer-linked selling appearing to block any significant upside progress, December appeared poised to test its recent low at 108.50 cents. Traders also noted chart objectives at 111, 109.10 and 109.70, while resistance was seen at 113.

Meanwhile, traders appeared unfazed by mounting political turmoil in Colombia, the world's second leading coffee producer. On Tuesday, the country's vice president, Humberto de la Calle, resigned, and urged President Samper to do the same.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
